_readme: REQUIRED-FENCE REGISTRY — the inverse of tools/retired-claims.json (check C1).
retired-claims.json catches a BANNED claim REAPPEARING. This catches a REQUIRED
safeguard GOING MISSING — the compression-drift failure this repo records over and
over: an essay says 'X is true, but only in this fenced sense', and the card /
mastery page / daily-arg keeps X and drops the fence, so a sentence that was safe in
the essay reads as heresy on its own screen.
Each rule says: these FILES make a claim that REQUIRES a fence, so each of them must
contain at least one of the `require` patterns (case-insensitive regexes, matched
against the served content — prose AND card/ARG_PREMISES script strings both count).
The content-review STAMP is stripped first, so a fence merely DOCUMENTED in the review
comment does not satisfy the rule; it must be in the reader-facing content. A file with
none of them has dropped the fence.
DISCIPLINE (identical to every other net here): a rule must pass on ALL current
content with ZERO gaps before it ships — a guard that fires on our own fenced pages
gets ignored. Scope `files` to pages that actually MAKE the claim (e.g. compassion.html
is NOT in the patripassianism rule — it never says the Son was executed, so it needs no
fence; adding it would false-fire). Seeded conservatively; add a rule only after
confirming every listed file currently passes (node tools/check-required-fences.mjs).
A genuinely fence-free exception is accepted on-record in required-fences-baseline.json.

rules.what: Any surface arguing eternal generation must fence the Son against derived/later/lesser deity (the Arian direction).
rules.instead: Carry one of: 'co-equal and co-eternal' / 'in no way later or lesser' / 'an eternal relation of origin' / 'God from God' / 'begotten, not made'.

rules.what: Any surface saying the Son or God was crucified/executed must fence patripassianism: the Son suffered in his assumed human nature; the divine nature did not die and the Father was not crucified.
rules.instead: Fence with the two-natures / communicatio idiomatum point: the eternal Son suffered in the human nature he assumed; the divine nature did not die and the Father was not crucified.

rules.what: Any surface running the Kalam cosmological argument must use the guarded premise 'whatever BEGINS TO EXIST has a cause', never the self-refuting 'everything has a cause'.
rules.instead: State premise 1 as 'whatever begins to exist has a cause of its existence' — the whole argument turns on the universe BEGINNING; 'everything has a cause' invites 'then what caused God?' and is not what the argument claims.

rules.what: Any fine-tuning surface must keep the data/design firewall: the DATA is conceded by atheist physicists; DESIGN is the contested, inferred conclusion — never 'scientists agree the universe is designed'.
rules.instead: Keep the two separate: the fine-tuning data is granted even by atheist physicists; that it points to a designer is a contested philosophical INFERENCE, not a scientific consensus.

rules.what: Any manuscript/textual-reliability surface must fence preservation from truth: the manuscripts show the text was accurately PRESERVED, not that its contents are TRUE — that is argued separately.
rules.instead: State plainly that textual evidence establishes accurate transmission, NOT the truth of what was transmitted; the truth of the content is a separate argument.

rules.what: The resurrection minimal-facts / creed surfaces must lead with the 1 Corinthians 15:3-7 pre-Pauline creed dated to within a few years of the crucifixion, never frame the evidence as merely 'written decades later'.
rules.instead: Anchor the case in the 1 Corinthians 15:3-7 formula Paul RECEIVED (pre-Pauline, traceable to within roughly two to five years of the crucifixion); do not let the Gospels' later composition date stand as the earliest evidence.
